channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Zema diz que se eleito à presidência do Brasil, vai "privatizar tudo"
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate and former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo-MG) stated that, if elected, he will privatize all state-owned companies under federal control. He claims this measure will help reduce Brazil's interest rates more quickly.

item.title: Malafaia diz que Bolsa Família impede Brasil de prosperar e critica o fim da escala 6×1
item.description: Pastor Silas Malafaia criticized the Bolsa Família program as vote-buying that hinders Brazil's prosperity and opposed the end of the 6×1 work schedule, claiming its supporters want to work one day and rest six. He also reiterated his criticism of the Supreme Federal Court (STF), claiming political persecution after being indicted for slander and arguing that the fake news inquiry is illegal and aims to silence critics. The service was attended by political figures including Flávio Bolsonaro, Cláudio Castro, and Sóstenes Cavalcante.

item.title: Redução de danos do vexame de Messias envolve abandono de Alexandre de Moraes
item.description: The defeat of Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF led Lula's allies to promote an alternative narrative claiming Alexandre de Moraes and Davi Alcolumbre blocked it due to interests in the Banco Master case. However, the text argues the Senate's rejection stemmed from broader concerns about Lula's pattern of prioritizing personal loyalty over institutional independence and Moraes' problematic ties to Banco Master, rendering the Moraes-Alcolumbre alliance a convenient but reductive explanation for a historically significant institutional rebuke.

item.title: Zema diz que vai ‘privatizar tudo’ se for eleito presidente do Brasil
item.description: Romeu Zema, pre-candidate for president and former governor of Minas Gerais, said that if elected, he would privatize all state-owned enterprises controlled by the federal government to rapidly reduce Brazil’s interest rates. He added that privatization would be accompanied by administrative, pension, and social benefit reforms, though he did not specify which companies would be targeted or the exact nature of the proposed reforms.

item.title: Fala de Zema sobre trabalho infantil repercute nas redes sociais
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), a pre-candidate for President, defended child labor during an interview on the Inteligência Ltda podcast, stating that children can help with simple tasks and citing the U.S. example where kids deliver newspapers. His remarks drew strong negative reactions from politicians like Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ), Pedro Roussef (PT-MG), and Minister Guilherme Boulos, who labeled the comments as retrograde, cowardly, and indicative of psychopathy.

item.title: TCU diz que cabe à Justiça Eleitoral analisar caso e arquiva pedido de apuração sobre uso de avião de Vorcaro por Nikolas
item.description: The TCU dismissed a request to investigate the use of Daniel Vorcaro's jet by federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira in 2022, stating the matter falls under Electoral Justice jurisdiction due to campaign-related expenses. The court found insufficient evidence of federal resource misuse and referred the case to the TSE and MPE for further review.

item.title: Bolsonaro tem boa evolução clínica e segue internado para reabilitação, diz boletim médico
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro remains hospitalized at DF Star Hospital in Brasília for rehabilitation following right shoulder surgery performed on Friday. According to a medical bulletin released on Sunday, he has shown good clinical progress, was able to eat soup, and moved the fingers of the operated hand. He is expected to be discharged on Monday. Bolsonaro is serving temporary house arrest at the Solar de Brasília condominium due to a 27-year-and-three-month sentence for crimes including attempted violent abolition of the democratic state.

item.title: Bolsonaro segue internado em hospital após cirurgia no ombro
item.description: Former President Jair Bolsonaro remains hospitalized at DF Star Hospital following shoulder surgery, authorized by STF Minister Alexandre de Moraes and endorsed by the PGR. He was serving a humanitarian house arrest sentence for a 27-year conviction related to an attempted coup, granted due to bilateral bacterial aspiration pneumonia. The surgery was completed without complications, focusing on pain management, thrombosis prevention, and motor rehabilitation.

item.title: Boletim atualiza estado clínico de Bolsonaro neste domingo; confira
item.description: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro is hospitalized at DF Star Hospital in Brasília following arthroscopic surgery on his right shoulder performed on Friday, May 1. According to a medical bulletin released on Sunday, May 3, he is showing good clinical progress, with pain under control and no complications, and is expected to be discharged on Monday, May 4. Bolsonaro is serving house arrest authorized by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes after being convicted of attempting a coup d'état.

item.title: Bolsonaro tem 'boa evolução clínica' após cirurgia no ombro, diz boletim médico
item.description: Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro is showing good clinical progress following arthroscopic surgery to repair the right rotator cuff, performed on Friday, May 1st. He remains hospitalized at DF Star Hospital for pain management, thrombosis prevention, and motor rehabilitation, with discharge expected on Monday, May 4th. The surgery was authorized by Supreme Court Minister Alexandre de Moraes, as Bolsonaro is currently serving a prison sentence for attempted coup under house arrest due to health reasons.

item.title: No 2º dia após cirurgia, Michelle diz que Bolsonaro tem dor controlada
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro reported that former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro has controlled pain and is showing good progress on the second day post-surgery for a right shoulder rotator cuff repair at DF Star Hospital in Brasília. He remains upset because he cannot feed himself due to the surgery on his dominant side, but is being assisted by his wife and monitored by medical staff, with no complications reported so far.

item.title: Elo com PT vira pedra no sapato de candidato que mira colar em Bolsonaro em Estado superbolsonarista
item.description: Adailton Fúria (PSD), a pre-candidate for governor of Rondônia, seeks to align himself with Jair Bolsonaro by sharing old videos, but faces backlash from Bolsonaro supporters after hiring a lawyer linked to the PT. He also attacked his rival Marcos Rogério (PL) for alleged left-wing ties, claiming he was part of Dilma’s base in the PDT. The race for Rondônia’s governorship intensifies as both candidates vie to associate themselves with the Bolsonaro family in a state where Bolsonaro received over 70% of the vote in 2022.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro participa de culto de “amigo” Malafaia
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) attended a service at the Assembleia de Deus Vitória em Cristo in Penha, Rio de Janeiro, alongside Pastor Silas Malafaia, signaling a reconciliation after months of political tensions. The meeting took place on Sunday, April 3, and suggests a potential realignment between the senator and one of Bolsonaro’s most influential evangelical allies.

item.title: Lula lembra centenário de geógrafo brasileiro Milton Santos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva commemorated the centenary of Brazilian geographer Milton Santos, emphasizing his importance in understanding globalization's inequalities and the transformative potential of peripheries. Lula stressed that Santos's thought remains relevant and necessary amid current geopolitical shifts, referencing his critique of globalization as a process that deepens local differences despite promises of homogenization.

item.title: Flávio defende redução da maioridade penal após estupro coletivo
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and other right-wing politicians advocated for lowering the age of criminal responsibility following a gang rape of two girls aged 7 and 10 in São Paulo, committed by four teenagers and one adult. Bolsonaro stated he supports reducing the age to 16 generally and to 14 in rape cases, referencing a constitutional amendment proposal (PEC) under Senate review. The incident sparked widespread social media debate, with backing from figures such as Nikolas Ferreira, Carlos Jordy, and Bombeiro Rafa, who stressed the urgency of addressing impunity among juvenile offenders.

item.title: Coordenador da campanha de Lula diz que Flávio Bolsonaro bateu no teto
item.description: Wellington Dias, coordinator of Lula's re-election campaign, says Flávio Bolsonaro's rise in polls stems from inheriting his father's political space but has plateaued for about 60 days. He claims Lula remains ahead in polling averages and predicts the 2026 election will be less tense than 2022, despite ongoing fake news and hatred. Dias emphasizes voters will prioritize substantive policy content, particularly stability, security, economic growth, and social improvement, resulting from the Lula government's revival of social programs.

item.title: Haddad usará caso do Banco Master para atacar Tarcísio de Freitas em SP
item.description: Fernando Haddad, the PT's pre-candidate for São Paulo governor, plans to use the Banco Master scandal to attack his rival Tarcísio de Freitas, emphasizing he never met Vorcaro or received illicit funds. The campaign will highlight that Bolsonaro received R$3 million and Tarcísio R$2 million from Vorcaro's relatives in 2022, mirroring the PT's national strategy against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Flávio se descola de Lula no Polymarket 10 dias após proibição
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) leads Polymarket betting odds for the 2026 Brazilian presidential election at 43.5%, surpassing Lula (PT) at 39% and Renan Santos (Missão) at 5.7%. This shift occurs ten days after a restriction related to the senator, indicating a divergence from Lula’s support in the prediction market. Former Governor Romeu Zema (Novo) previously peaked at 10% but declined following conflicts with Supreme Court justices.

item.title: Biógrafo diz acreditar que Lula será reeleito no 1º turno
item.description: Journalist Fernando Morais believes Lula will be re-elected in the first round of 2026 if the right remains fragmented. He argues Lula has a history of overcoming early polling deficits and remains confident the president can turn the current technical tie with Flávio Bolsonaro into victory.

item.title: CEOs encaram 2026 em modo defensivo e acreditam em mudança de governo
item.description: Brazilian CEOs approach 2026 defensively, prioritizing operational efficiency, deleveraging, and cash preservation amid expectations of political change. Most anticipate a runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, favoring the opposition, and expect the next government to prioritize fiscal balance over interest rate cuts or administrative reform.

item.title: Lula saiu da prisão melhor do que entrou, diz biógrafo
item.description: Biographer Fernando Morais claims Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s imprisonment from 2018 to 2021 led to a positive transformation, deepening his class consciousness and anti-imperialist views. During 581 days in Curitiba, Lula engaged in intensive reading, received weekly visits from Janja, and refused to seek pardon or amnesty. His release followed STF rulings and the annulment of convictions due to bias in the Lava Jato operation.

item.title: Eleição de 2026 terá recorde de idosos; jovens recuam
item.description: The 2026 elections will feature a record number of elderly voters, with 23.2% of registered voters aged 60 or older — up 7.9 percentage points since 2010. Meanwhile, voters aged 16 to 24 have declined from 18.2% to 12.0% over the same period, and recent polls show Lula’s advantage among youth narrowing to a technical tie, while among seniors, results show either a tie or a slight edge for Lula against Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vai a culto de Malafaia para reconciliação após atritos no início do ano
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro attended a service at Pastor Silas Malafaia’s church, marking a reconciliation after earlier tensions over Flávio’s designation as Jair Bolsonaro’s successor. The gathering included key PL allies such as Cláudio Castro, Douglas Ruas, Marcelo Crivella and others, signaling unity and a potential explicit endorsement from Malafaia for Flávio’s candidacy.

item.title: O tsunami de pesquisas sobre a eleição para presidente em 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) was flooded with records of presidential election opinion polls for 2026 in the first four months of this electoral year, reflecting intense public and media interest in the race. The subscriber-only article describes this 'tsunami' of data as an indicator of the expected polarization and competitiveness in the upcoming election. Full access requires registration via the article’s link.

item.title: PSB de Tebet quer dobradinha em chapa de Lula ao Senado em SP
item.description: Simone Tebet confirmed she will not be Lula's vice-presidential candidate, honoring the agreement to run for Senate in São Paulo. Her party, the PSB, is also demanding the second senatorial slot on Lula's ticket for Márcio França, aiming for a double Senate candidacy in SP. The report is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: Rejeição de Jorge Messias vira trunfo eleitoral para senadores conservadores
item.description: Conservative senators from right-leaning states took advantage of the rejection of Lula's Supreme Court nominee, Jorge Messias, to film themselves celebrating in the Senate plenary, turning the episode into an electoral strategy for the 2026 elections. An ally of Messias observed the move, noting that colleagues were leveraging the backlash against the federal government to gain voter support. The report highlights that the gesture was used to gain visibility and votes among conservative-leaning electors.

item.title: PL da Dosimetria não causa insegurança jurídica, dizem especialistas
item.description: Experts say the Dosimetry Bill, approved by Congress after a partial veto by Lula, does not create direct legal insecurity with the Anti-Faction Bill, as they address distinct topics: crimes against the democratic state (e.g., coup attempts) versus organized crime. However, the Senate president’s decision to split the veto may be challenged in court, and the law could benefit those investigated for the January 8 events, including Jair Bolsonaro, by allowing retroactive application favorable to the defendant.

item.title: Bolsonaro "menos" preso, mas ainda fora da urna
item.description: Despite the reduction of Jair Bolsonaro's prison sentence, which could allow him to transition to open regime by 2028, he remains ineligible and out of the 2026 electoral race. The article emphasizes that congressional defeats for Lula's government do not determine election outcomes, as voters prioritize economic conditions and personal finances over technical votes in Brasília. While the opposition seeks to frame the government as weakened, the real political battle is decided in the daily lives of workers.

item.title: Filme ‘A Sombra do Meu Pai’ ecoa drama de ‘Ainda Estou Aqui’ na Nigéria
item.description: The Nigerian-British film ‘A Sombra do Meu Pai’ follows two boys who, during Nigeria’s 1993 military coup that annulled presidential elections, experience the sudden return of their absent father and a turbulent journey through Lagos, blending family drama and political unrest to explore lost innocence and masculinity. Directed by Akinola Davies Jr., the Cannes and BAFTA-awarded film draws parallels with Brazilian hits like ‘Ainda Estou Aqui’ and ‘O Agente Secreto’, using fiction to reconstruct the paternal figure the director lost as a toddler to an epileptic crisis.

item.title: Inflação volta a ganhar força no Brasil e complica planos de acelerar corte de juros
item.description: Inflation in Brazil has surged again in 2026, driven by the escalation of the Iran conflict, which pushed up oil prices and affected fuels and freight, creating broad inflationary pressure. This complicates plans by the Lula government and the Central Bank to accelerate interest rate cuts, keeping credit expensive and eroding household purchasing power in an election year.

item.title: A analogia futebolística de um aliado de Lula para se queixar da estratégia de poupar Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: A Lula ally running for Senate in Brazil's Northeast criticized the government and PT's strategy of sparing Flávio Bolsonaro in recent months, using a football analogy: 'I don't understand why let the opponent go up 2-0 just to have to chase and try to come back.' He argues this allows rivals like Tarcísio de Freitas to gain political advantage unchallenged. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia prepara proposta de código de conduta que deve circular ainda no primeiro semestre
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia is preparing a code of conduct proposal for Supreme Court justices, expected to be circulated in the first semester. Although STF President Edson Fachin acknowledges the code has little chance of being approved before the 2026 elections, he is betting on initial steps that could be taken by October. The article is exclusive to subscribers.

item.title: A aposta da campanha de Haddad para desgatar Tarcísio com as mulheres
item.description: Fernando Haddad's (PT) campaign plans to exploit a 45% increase in femicide cases in São Paulo in February 2026 to undermine Governor Tarcísio de Freitas's (Republicans) image, proposing extended hours for women's police stations and offering shelters and job market access for victims. The strategy targets the decline in Tarcísio's approval among women, which dropped from 57% to 48% over the last eight months, according to Genial/Quaest polls. In response, the governor is appointing women to key positions, including the first female commander of the Military Police, to counteract the backlash.

item.title: Desenrola 2.0: entenda novo programa e seu papel na estratégia de Lula para 2026
item.description: President Lula's government will launch 'Desenrola 2.0' on April 4, offering debt discounts of 20% to 90% for high-interest debts like credit cards and overdrafts, with FGTS funds available for repayment. Led by Finance Minister Dario Durigan, the program aims to improve Lula's image amid high indebtedness affecting 81.7 million Brazilians, positioning it as a key electoral strategy for 2026. It operates through public guarantees to banks, not direct Treasury spending, enabling them to offer deep discounts while assuming repayment risk.

item.title: Flamengo tem defesa sólida contra o Vasco e vira boa opção de aposta
item.description: Flamengo enters the Brasileiro derby against Vasco as the clear favorite with 1.49 odds to win, backed by a strong defensive record in recent matches, including four clean sheets in six wins over the last ten encounters. Vasco, at 5.91 odds, aims to end a three-year winless streak against their rivals. Key betting options include Flamengo winning without conceding (2.36) or winning while conceding (1.52).

item.title: O cronograma de Hugo Motta para a escala 6x1
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB) aims to approve the PEC on the 6×1 work scale by the end of this month, leveraging Labor Day mobilization. Rapporteur Deputy Leo Prates (Republicanos-BA) is expected to present his report on Tuesday (May 5), with committee voting scheduled for May 25–26 and floor consideration on May 27. Motta reaffirmed his commitment to workers, stating the process will be concluded in May.

item.title: Agrishow: de olho no Planalto, pré-candidatos de direita disputam preferência do agro
item.description: Right-wing pre-candidates, including Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos), vied for agribusiness support at the Agrishow in Ribeirão Preto, aiming to strengthen their 2026 presidential campaigns. Despite public appearances and supporter engagement, they did not present concrete policy proposals for the sector during the event. Tarcísio endorsed Bolsonaro’s legacy and projected Flávio as the next president, while allies debate the timing of his formal endorsement.

item.title: Saiba qual é a posição do Brasil em rankings de democracia e governança
item.description: Brazil is classified as an 'imperfect electoral democracy' and 'free' by leading global indices on democracy and governance released in 2025–2026, including the V-Dem Democracy Report, Freedom in the World, Economist Democracy Index, and Global State of Democracy. In governance, rule of law, and justice indicators — such as the World Bank’s Worldwide Governance Indicators, Bertelsmann Transformation Index, Human Freedom Index, Economic Freedom of the World, and WJP Rule of Law Index — the country scores in the intermediate to high range, reflecting progress in some areas alongside enduring challenges in institutional effectiveness and the rule of law.

item.title: Bolsonaristas apontam as duas agendas de Trump que podem ajudar Flávio
item.description: Bolsonarist leaders believe two Trump administration agendas could benefit Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 elections: the reinstatement of the Magnitsky Act against Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes and the designation of PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations. While rejecting a direct public endorsement from Trump, they see these measures as strategic to bolster Flávio’s discourse and attract voter support.

item.title: A rendição do Senado
item.description: The Brazilian Congress approved the overturning of the veto on the Dosimetry Bill, reducing penalties for those who attacked democracy on January 8, marking a symbolic victory for Bolsonarism. The image of Senator Davi Alcolumbre being embraced by Flávio Bolsonaro symbolized the Senate's surrender to a project favoring coup plotters, despite Lula's rejection of Jorge Messias for the Supreme Court. International press, including the Washington Post, warns this decision could overturn the 2026 elections and reveals a fragile relationship between the government and Congress.

item.title: Crise entre Planalto e presidente do Senado deixa a federação União-PP mais perto de apoiar Flávio
item.description: The rejection of Jorge Messias to the STF deepened the crisis between the Planalto and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, who has moved closer to Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula’s main presidential rival. Five months ahead of the 2026 elections, this tension raises the likelihood of União-PP backing Bolsonaro’s candidacy.

item.title: Entrevista: ‘Lula sabia do risco, e decisão de ir até o fim foi consciente ’, diz líder do governo sobre Messias
item.description: The government leader admitted that the rejection of Jorge Messias's nomination to the STJ by the Senate was anticipated, citing articulation difficulties in a Congress with a conservative majority and electoral calendar pressure. Despite internal optimistic projections of 43 to 45 favorable votes, the result was 34, reflecting an underestimation of Bolsonarist opposition, which controls around 35 senators. He stated he had warned Minister Messias and President Lula about the vote's unviability since November, but the decision to proceed was upheld by the majority of the base leaders.

item.title: Elio Gaspari: os saltos altos quebram
item.description: The nomination of Jorge Messias to the Supreme Federal Court (STF) was seen as the peak of PT influence in Lula 3.0, but his rejection marked the end of that dominance. The following day, the overturning of the dosimetry veto further weakened the STF’s position, signaling a shift in the balance of power. The subscriber-exclusive article frames this moment as the symbolic collapse of the 'high heel' of the petista establishment.

item.title: ‘O voto nos estados’: com segurança e privatizações no centro da revanche, Tarcísio e Haddad reeditam disputa em SP
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas and Fernando Haddad are renewing their 2022 rivalry for the São Paulo governorship in 2026, centering the debate on Sabesp’s privatization and public security. A Genial/Quaest poll shows Tarcísio leading with 38% of voting intentions versus Haddad’s 26%, mirroring the 2022 gap. The Sabesp privatization, completed in June 2024, is framed by Tarcísio as an achievement and by Haddad as a source of public dissatisfaction, tied to rising complaints at Arsep and Procon.

item.title: Derrotas no Congresso estremecem base de Lula para tentativa de reeleição e testam relação entre Poderes
item.description: Seven months from the end of his third term, Lula faces his worst relationship with Congress, marked by tensions with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, threatening the approval of strategic agendas like ending the 6x1 work scale and the Public Security PEC. The government fears parliamentary retaliation, including the passage of 'bomb' bills, in a critical election year for his reelection bid.

item.title: Presiones de Trump, tretas partidistas y supresión del voto negro: la batalla sin cuartel por las elecciones de noviembre en EE UU
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court, with a conservative majority, struck down a Louisiana electoral district with a Black majority, further weakening the Voting Rights Act of 1965. The ruling opens the door to electoral rule changes in other Southern states that could favor the Republican Party by making it harder for Black citizens to vote.

item.title: Conservadorismo não é bolsonarismo
item.description: The text argues that conservatism in Brazil is an older, broader, and deeper political and intellectual tradition, while Bolsonarism is a recent, personalist political phenomenon centered on Jair Bolsonaro’s figure, rhetoric, method, and surrounding community. It criticizes the common conflation of the two as analytically flawed. The content is presented as exclusive subscriber material.

item.title: Ivan Valente se despede do Congresso e prega guinada de Lula à esquerda
item.description: Ivan Valente, a PSOL deputy, delivered his final speech in Congress on March 19, announcing his retirement at age 80 after eight terms. He denounced corruption among PL deputies, criticized 'elite lackeys,' and condemned figures like Flávio Bolsonaro and Nikolas Ferreira, lamenting the decline of political discourse and the normalization of the January 8 coup attempt. His farewell reflected on the need for political renewal and his lifelong struggle against dictatorship and for the left.

item.title: Indicação de Messias foi ponto alto da onipotência petista, e saltos altos quebraram
item.description: The nomination of Jorge Messias to the Supreme Federal Court was seen as the peak of petista omnipotence during Lula 3.0. His rejection marked the moment when the government's perceived invincibility was broken, symbolized by a broken high heel. The following day, the overturning of the dosimetry veto represented another defeat, with the 'Supreme Court's heel' also breaking.

item.title: Lula testa mote para reeleição enquanto acumula tropeços no Congresso
item.description: President Lula (PT) is testing a campaign slogan for his 2026 re-election bid amid growing difficulties with Congress. Last week, he suffered two significant defeats, including the historic rejection of his Supreme Court nominee — the first since the late 19th century. These legislative setbacks complicate his agenda and increase pressure on his candidacy.
